domain_setting: A clear association-football match in a green stadium: visible touchlines, halfway and penalty markings, goal frames with nets, a patterned round soccer ball, and distinct player roles. Use safe fair play and respectful crowd and officiating scenes.

ambient_palette.field: fresh grass green, chalk white, quiet stadium sage
ambient_palette.players: two contrasting kit colors with dark slate outlines
ambient_palette.equipment: warm ivory ball, pale net, amber corner flag and cards
ambient_palette.time_and_results: cool field tones, restrained board marks and bright whistle/referee details

recurring_scale_anchors: Canvas 304×192; keep goal frames, players, balls, and flags within the safe area.
A soccer ball should be round and visibly patterned, distinct from the oval American-football ball.
Use readable full-size goal frames and nets; distinguish field lines, touchline, penalty box, center circle, and corner arc.
Player-role cards should show soccer context and different positions relative to a goal; do not rely on uniforms or readable numbers.
For cards and discipline, depict calm officiating and safe exits; avoid rough contact, injury detail, or humiliating behavior.
Use no text, readable numbers, logos, or club marks.

polysemy_resolution_table.soccer: Association football with round ball, rectangular goal and net; distinct from American football in Lesson 60.
polysemy_resolution_table.ball: Round patterned soccer ball, not a basketball or American-football oval.
polysemy_resolution_table.field / pitch: Marked grass soccer playing surface; pitch means the soccer field, not tar residue.
polysemy_resolution_table.goal / score a goal: Goal is the scoring target/result; score a goal is the action of sending the ball into the net.
polysemy_resolution_table.corner / corner kick: Corner is the field corner arc/flag area; corner kick is the restart taken from that arc.
polysemy_resolution_table.penalty / penalty spot: Penalty is the awarded kick after a foul; penalty spot is the marked location from which it is taken.
polysemy_resolution_table.tie / draw: Equal-score soccer match result, not tying a knot.
polysemy_resolution_table.lose: Lose the match respectfully, not lose an object.
polysemy_resolution_table.forward / striker / midfielder / defende: Distinct soccer positions: midfield between boxes, defender closer to own goal, forward in attacking third, striker central nearest opponent goal.
polysemy_resolution_table.manager: Soccer team manager directing team tactics, not a shop or company manager.
polysemy_resolution_table.net / bar / goalpost: Net is the mesh behind the goal opening; bar is the crossbar; goalpost is either vertical upright.
polysemy_resolution_table.full time / halftime / injury time / sto: Separate match periods and time additions: halftime break, full time/end, injury time added for injury delays, stoppage time broader added time for match delays.
polysemy_resolution_table.be booked / booked / red card / be sent: Yellow card is a caution/booked; red card is the object; be sent off is the referee action, sent off is the player leaving after dismissal.
polysemy_resolution_table.kick / kickoff / throw-in / free kick: Separate soccer actions and restarts: kick contacts the ball, kickoff starts/restarts at center, throw-in restarts from touchline, free kick follows a foul.
polysemy_resolution_table.goalkeeper / goalie: Keeper guarding the goal mouth with gloves and body positioned to block a shot.
polysemy_resolution_table.linesman / referee: Linesman assistant follows the touchline with a flag; referee is central official with whistle and cards.
polysemy_resolution_table.fans / mascot / steward / security: Fans watch and cheer from stands; mascot is a costumed team character; steward guides spectators; security staff calmly protect the venue.
polysemy_resolution_table.substitutes: Players waiting at sideline/bench to replace an on-field teammate.
